notes: Round 11. Added a real CLI (12 tests, smoke-tested) and ran the final security gate the owner asked for. SEC-STRIX-001 was an independent read-only review by a separate model: docs/SECURITY-REVIEW.md carries 11 findings with path:line evidence. The four I re-verified myself and the two most severe: (S1, Critical) tauri.conf.json had "csp": null so the webview ran with no Content-Security-Policy; (S2, High) RedirectTracker::step enforced scheme/hop/loop/credential-stripping but had no private-target guard, so a public server could pivot the app onto a LAN or loopback service; (S3) neutralize_reserved_device_names only compared text before the first dot, so `CON .txt` slipped through; (S4) is_disallowed_char filtered C0/DEL but not bidi overrides or zero-width characters; (S5) engine.rs:213 called .lock().unwrap() where the six other sites handle poisoning. SEC-FIX-001 remediated all of them plus download-dir validation, store-path re-sanitization, noreferrer links, and a vitest 5 upgrade: sayl-http 65->68 tests, sayl-app 9->11, npm audit 3 advisories -> 0. Residual risks are documented in the review's accepted-risks section: the CSP is set but cannot be proven enforced without a WebView2 runtime, DNS-rebinding pivots after the redirect check are uncovered, and store files inherit the default DACL. Earlier rounds: toolchain solved with GNU+rust-lld (MSVC lacks the Windows SDK), state-machine self-transition fix, fixture server, HTTP-001/002, STORE-001, APP-001, SITE-001, UI-001, DOCS-001, REL-001. 150 crate tests plus 21 frontend tests are green; totals now core 33, test-http 25, http 68, storage 18, app 11, cli 12, desktop 3 (unrunnable locally), frontend 21.
